title: Antimicrobial Activity Assay
author: Bie Ekblad
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.i66chhe
materials: Thaw peptides of choice on ice

steps.title: Prepare overnight indicator culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate the indicator strain into approximately 1 ml of appropriate growth medium (volume may be adjusted to the amount needed the next day). Incubate overnight (o/n) at the desired temperature, with or without agitation as required for the strain.

steps.title: Calculate peptide volume for first well
steps.instruction: Determine the volume of peptide stock to add so that the first well of the second row contains the target concentration in 200 µl total volume. Example: to obtain 50 nM final peptide from a 50 µM stock, prepare a 0.2 µM solution in 50 µl medium (0.05 µM × 200 µl = 0.2 µM × 50 µl). Because each row receives an extra 50 µl of medium during the dilution series, aim for 0.2 µM in 100 µl (0.2 µM × 100 µl = 0.4 µl peptide). Thus add 0.4 µl of the 50 µM stock to the first well of each row (or calculate the volume for 200 µl and double it).

steps.title: Add growth medium to assay wells
steps.instruction: Dispense 50 µl of fresh growth medium into every well of each row that will be used. The first row (wells 1A‑12A) receives only medium and the indicator cells; no peptide is added to this row.

steps.title: Add calculated peptide to first well
steps.instruction: Pipette the peptide volume calculated in step 2 into the first well of each row (the well that will start the dilution series). Mix gently by pipetting up and down.

steps.title: Perform two‑fold serial dilution across row
steps.instruction: Serially dilute the peptide across the row:

substeps.instruction: Transfer 50 µl from the first well to the second well of the same row and mix by pipetting up and down 6–8 times.
Repeat the transfer‑mix cycle from each well to the next until the final well of the row is reached.
After the last transfer, discard the remaining 50 µl in the final well so that every well now contains 50 µl (peptide + medium) representing a two‑fold dilution series.

steps.title: Dilute overnight culture to working concentration
steps.instruction: Dilute the overnight indicator culture with fresh growth medium either 1:50 (for daytime incubation) or 1:200 (for overnight incubation), depending on the planned incubation length.

steps.title: Add diluted culture to each well
steps.instruction: Add 150 µl of the diluted overnight culture to every well of each row, bringing the total volume in each well to 200 µl. Begin adding the culture to the most diluted well (e.g., well 12) and proceed toward the less diluted wells.

steps.title: Incubate microtiter plate
steps.instruction: Seal the plate with its lid and incubate at the temperature and for the duration appropriate for the indicator strain and experimental design.

steps.title: Prepare background control and measure OD600

substeps.instruction: Remove the entire solution from well 1A, wash the well, and add 200 µl of fresh growth medium from the same batch (well 1A now serves as the background control).
Measure the optical density at 600 nm (OD₆₀₀) in a microtiter‑plate reader, ensuring that a shaking step is included in the program to disperse cells before reading.
Subtract the OD value of well 1A (background) from all other wells.
Calculate the average OD of the indicator cells without peptide (the first row). Divide this average by two to obtain the ½ max growth value (e.g., 0.15).

Locate the row where the ½ max value lies; it will be between two adjacent wells (e.g., wells 5B and 6B). Record the OD of these two wells (e.g., 5B = 0.112, 6B = 0.215) and their peptide concentrations (e.g., 5B = 3.125 nM, 6B = 1.563 nM).
Calculate ΔC (difference in concentration) = 3.125 nM − 1.563 nM = 1.563 nM and ΔOD = 0.215 − 0.112 = 0.103.
Compute the fraction‑OD: (OD₅B − ½ max) / ΔOD = (0.112 − 0.15) / 0.103 ≈ 0.103 (as given).
Determine the MIC: concentration of the first well minus (fraction‑OD × ΔC) = 3.125 nM − (0.103 × 1.563 nM) ≈ 2.95 nM ≈ 3 nM.
Report the MIC₅₀ as the average of at least three independent measurements performed at different time points.

steps.title: Add growth medium to first column (100 µl)
steps.instruction: Add growth medium to each well of the first column (column A) so that the final volume in those wells is 100 µl. Mix gently by pipetting up and down 6–8 times.
